Folks — I ran a quick model-footprint write-up and a pair of capacity scenarios. I put the numbers in the attached sizing workbook (peregrine_sizing_model.xlsx) and summarized the key assumptions below.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model: Peregrine-7B-32k architecture; FP16 dense weights baseline ≈ 14 GB resident on GPU.
- Quantization: int8 reduces weight footprint to ~5.5–6.0 GB (includes some extra dequant buffers); int4 ~3.2–3.8 GB with per-layer quant artifacts and slightly higher CPU decode overhead.
- KV cache: grows linearly with context length. For this architecture, full 32k context KV cache ≈ 18–26 GB per replica (we tested similar 7B-class models). KV dominates total working set at long contexts. Estimates depend on layer count and key/value projection sizes; workbook documents per-layer math.
- Typical request mix: 60% short (<2k tokens), 30% mid (2–8k), 10% long (8k–32k) but long ones are expensive and cause transient memory pressure. Average active token window we modeled ~4k.
- Concurrency target: steady 40, peak 120 (bursty). SLOs: 99th < 750ms.

Scenario A — Performance-first (targeting H100 80GB):
- Config: Peregrine int8 (weights) + KV in-GPU where possible.
- Per-replica GPU working set: weights (~6 GB) + KV (avg 8–12 GB depending on active window) + activations/batch buffers (~6 GB) => ~20–26 GB usable. With H100-80 (80 GB) we can place 2–3 replicas per GPU depending on safety headroom and multiplexing.
- For steady 40 concurrent sessions (with amortized batching) we estimate 3 H100s (2 replicas per GPU, autoscale headroom) to meet latency SLOs. For 120 peak concurrency, add 2 more H100s for headroom (total 5 H100).
- Comments: In-GPU KV gives lowest latency because no PCIe/host roundtrip for long prefixes; higher cost but simpler concurrency behavior.

Scenario B — Cost-optimised (A10G-class, KV offload):
- Config: Peregrine int4 weights (~3.5 GB) + KV offloaded to host RAM (NVMe warm-up for long contexts).
- Per-replica GPU working set: weights (~3.5 GB) + activations (~6–8 GB) => ~12 GB. A10Gs with 24 GB can host 1 replica per GPU comfortably for short/mid requests; for long-context requests we rely on a hybrid flow: most traffic hits in-GPU short contexts, long requests cause an async offload with higher tail latency.
- For steady 40 concurrency (mixed traffic) we estimate 12 A10Gs (sharded across nodes with KV offload and aggressive batching). Peak 120 would need autoscale to ~25 A10Gs or fall back to queued long requests.
- Comments: This approach is ~2–3x cheaper but requires acceptance of higher 99th latency on long-context requests and more complex operational playbooks (KV eviction, prefetching).

Operational recommendations:
- Canary: start with 2x H100 for 30 days, run representative traffic and collect p50/p90/p99 and KV residency stats. If long-context traffic is >8% of total, prefer H100 path.
- Quantization plan: test int8 first — it gives a large weight reduction with minimal latency impact. Test int4 only if int8 meets quality gates; int4 can save additional GPU memory but may increase CPU decode time and complexity in fallback paths.
- KV strategies: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes (they mentioned heavy prefix reuse). Implement a dynamic KV cutoff: keep recent N tokens in-GPU and offload tail. Use warm-up/async prefetch for expected long requests.
- Model variants: serve a smaller context model variant for short flows (e.g., 8k-optimized) and route long flows to the 32k-capable pool to reduce average memory footprint and increase multiplexing.

Numbers summary (pilot):
- Performance-first pilot: 3 H100s baseline, scale to 5 for peak.
- Cost-optimised pilot: 12 A10Gs baseline, scale to ~25 for peak.

I'll attach the workbook with per-layer constants and detailed per-GPU occupancy math. Happy to go through the sheet with Peregrine engineers.
